facts.title: KAP: Bridging the Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption Gap in LLM Systems
facts.event_hint: Research paper presents KAP (Knowledge Access Planning), a paradigm-shifting execution abstraction for LLM serving that bridges the gap between structured knowledge priors and runtime KV consumption
facts.problem: The Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption (KSRC) gap: modern LLM systems produce high-value structured priors (ranked evidence, graph topology, multimodal alignment, confidence signals) but LLM serving backends observe only flat token sequences after prompt serialization, forcing dense and uniform consumption of full KV state during decoding. This increases latency and degrades throughput even when reasoning depends on only a small fraction of context
facts.mechanism: KAP elevates structured knowledge priors from passive prompt-construction hints into first-class physical execution artifacts through a universal intermediate representation - the runtime access plan - which compiles structured knowledge signals to govern physical KV access without altering logical prompt semantics, model weights, or training procedures. Instantiated as GraphSpec compiler-executor connecting Graph-RAG knowledge selection to vLLM serving backend, shifting LLM serving from token-aware context consumption to plan-driven, knowledge-aware runtime consumption

evidence.claim: GraphSpec reduces proposal-time KV access to 5.5% of source KV state at 128K context length
evidence.condition: 128K context length, long-context QA workload on SPIQA dataset

evidence.claim: GraphSpec achieves 1.08x-1.19x decode throughput speedup over full-context baseline across 4K-128K context lengths
evidence.baseline: Full-context decoding with standard vLLM backend
evidence.condition: SPIQA dataset, 4K-128K context lengths, decode throughput (TPS) measurement

evidence.claim: GraphSpec Top-3 tolerant acceptance rate remains high (0.953-0.962) across all context lengths, indicating proposal effectiveness
evidence.condition: 4K-128K context lengths, Top-3 tolerant proposal acceptance rate metric

evidence.claim: GraphSpec maintains answer quality comparable to full-context decoding, with pass rates differing by at most 1.9 percentage points at 64K (87.9% vs 86.0%)
evidence.condition: 64K context length, LLM similarity pass rate with 0.5 threshold

evidence.claim: Physical concat (prompt materialization without runtime access plan) achieves only 73.9% pass rate vs GraphSpec 87.9% at 64K, proving runtime access plan is essential
evidence.condition: 64K context length, same evidence selected but materialized as shortened prompt

facts.evaluation_context: Evaluated on SPIQA dataset with 4K-128K context lengths using vLLM serving backend. Graph-RAG evidence and priors frozen before benchmarking; frontend retrieval excluded from TTFT measurements. LLM-as-judge quality metric with 0.5 threshold independently validated (95% judge-human agreement on 100 sampled answers). Throughput covers complete executor path, not isolated model-forward performance
facts.limitations: Evaluation validates KAP through GraphSpec, a single concrete instantiation with Graph-RAG frontend and vLLM backend. Results strongest for long-context QA workloads where graph-derived priors can be grounded in evidence spans. Effectiveness depends on quality of knowledge priors, compiler's ability to translate into useful runtime access plans, and backend's ability to execute plans without excessive metadata/synchronization overhead. Other KAP instantiations may use different frontends, compilers, access policies, or backends
facts.project_relevance: Directly relevant to AI infrastructure horizontal tracking: addresses fundamental architectural mismatch in LLM serving systems, provides concrete system mechanism (runtime access plan IR), demonstrates end-to-end efficiency gains (1.08x-1.19x speedup) with quality preservation. Should be categorized under 'serving_runtime_compiler' direction. Represents paradigm shift from token-aware to knowledge-aware runtime consumption

facts.title: Kioxia and SanDisk 10th-Gen 332-Layer QLC NAND Achieves Industry's Highest Bit Density
facts.event_hint: Kioxia and Sandisk unveil 10th-generation 332-layer QLC 3D flash memory at FMS 2026 (August 4, 2026), claiming the industry's highest bit density for QLC NAND.
facts.problem: AI training, inference and hyperscale datacenter workloads drive unprecedented data growth, pressuring flash storage to deliver greater capacity, higher performance and improved energy efficiency simultaneously, while AI/cloud infrastructure faces power and cooling limits.
facts.mechanism: CMOS directly Bonded to Array (CBA) architecture fabricates CMOS logic and the memory array on separate wafers then bonds them with high-precision wafer-to-wafer alignment; a 332-layer optimized floorplan raises bit density; Toggle DDR6.0 plus the Separate Command Address (SCA) protocol enables a faster interface; Power-Isolated Low-Tapped Termination (PI-LTT) improves I/O data-out transfer power efficiency.

evidence.claim: The 10th-gen QLC 3D flash delivers up to a 60% increase in bit density versus the 8th-generation, surpassing 37 Gb/mm^2, presented as the industry benchmark for QLC bit density.
evidence.condition: QLC; vendor survey as of August 3, 2026
evidence.source_locator: Press release lede + 'Key ... highlights' bullet - 332-layer architecture / bit density

evidence.claim: It is the industry's first QLC 3D flash memory technology to reach a 4.8 Gb/s NAND interface, enabled by Toggle DDR6.0 and the Separate Command Address (SCA) protocol.
evidence.condition: Vendor test environment (value may vary by use); 1 Gb/s = 1,000,000,000 bits/s
evidence.source_locator: Press release lede + 'Key ... highlights' bullet - 4.8 Gb/s NAND interface

evidence.claim: The new generation improves read and write bandwidth compared to the 8th-generation 3D flash memory.
evidence.source_locator: Press release lede - CBA technology paragraph

evidence.claim: CMOS-directly-Bonded-to-Array (CBA) architecture enhances density scaling, performance, and manufacturing efficiency; Power-Isolated Low-Tapped Termination (PI-LTT) improves I/O data-out transfer power efficiency.
evidence.condition: CBA: CMOS and cell array wafers manufactured separately then bonded; PI-LTT for I/O power
evidence.source_locator: 'Key ... highlights' bullets - CBA architecture and PI-LTT

facts.evaluation_context: Joint Kioxia/Sandisk press release issued at Future of Memory and Storage (FMS) 2026, Santa Clara, August 4, 2026. 'Industry's highest' is a Kioxia/Sandisk survey claim as of August 3, 2026. Interface speed obtained under a vendor-specific test environment; no end-system or SSD-level benchmark results are provided.
facts.limitations: No absolute die capacity (Gb), P/E endurance, write amplification, access latency, or absolute read/write bandwidth (GB/s) are given. No sampling or mass-production timing is stated (Kioxia says it will 'accelerate development toward the commercialization'). The PI-LTT power-efficiency gain is qualitative only (no multiplier or percentage). 'Industry's highest bit density' is a vendor self-survey claim.
facts.project_relevance: Strongly relevant to storage_media density/bandwidth/power evidence: >37 Gb/mm^2 and a 4.8 Gb/s interface are concrete QLC density and interface advances, while CBA plus PI-LTT target the power/cooling constraints of AI infrastructure. However, missing endurance, absolute bandwidth and volume timing currently limit any assessment of deployable performance or cost/bit gain.
source_notes: 'Industry's highest bit density for QLC NAND' is a Kioxia/Sandisk self-survey as of August 3, 2026; 4.8 Gb/s measured under vendor-specific test environment.

facts.title: Fractal KV-Cache Archives: Lossless Symbolic Storage with In-Place Retrieval for Long-Context LLM Inference
facts.event_hint: arXiv research paper on fractal-based KV cache compression archive format
facts.problem: KV cache dominates memory cost of long-context autoregressive inference; existing compression (quantization, eviction, offloading) addresses the lossy compression step, but the question of how to store the resulting symbol stream and whether the storage layer can enable retrieval and random access remains unaddressed.
facts.mechanism: Contractive iterated-map codes (chaos game representation/universal sequence maps) serialize symbol sequences into low-dimensional real vectors, forming a lossless archive with O(1) random access, O(1) amortized append, linear-time encoding, and in-place substring search capability on stored vectors.

evidence.claim: Per-head residual VQ with hybrid bit allocation (K×4, V×2) achieves 36× compression vs fp16 at +11.2% perplexity cost
evidence.condition: GPT-2 124M, 1024-token context, 4-sink + 32-recent exact window, The Time Machine corpus

evidence.claim: Quantizing keys is ~4× more damaging to perplexity than quantizing values
evidence.baseline: values-only quantization (+4.0% perplexity) vs keys-only quantization (+14.5% perplexity)
evidence.condition: GPT-2, 1024-token context, per-head RVQ k=256×2 base configuration
evidence.source_locator: Table 2 and surrounding text, PDF Page 4

evidence.claim: Encoding performance: 0.68µs/char, 311µs random access lookup, 175µs/token append
Per-head codebooks Pareto-dominate pooled codebooks at equal bit budget
Archive supports approximate substring queries directly on stored vectors with full recall
evidence.baseline: sequential decoding required for arithmetic coding
evidence.condition: Stored vectors enable nearest-neighbor distance as graded suffix-similarity

facts.evaluation_context: GPT-2 (124M parameters), The Time Machine corpus (public domain), 1024-token contexts, single laptop CPU, exact window = 4 attention sinks + 32 recent tokens (3.5% of context at 1024), perplexity as sole quality metric, exact baseline perplexity = 35.97, codebooks trained on disjoint span of same book via k-means
facts.limitations: Small-scale study on single 124M-parameter model; only perplexity measured (no downstream task accuracy); per-head codebooks trained per-corpus not amortized; retrieval limited to suffix matching not semantic retrieval; serialization advantage is access pattern not compression ratio (uniform code 6.13 bits/char vs ~2.55 bits/char for order-2 model); larger models may tolerate more KV quantization but unvalidated
facts.project_relevance: Relevant to cross-domain cache transfer as the fractal archive format provides: (1) high compression (36×) enabling lower bandwidth transfer of archived KV states; (2) O(1) random access enabling selective retrieval rather than full-cache transfer; (3) in-place search index for matching cached contexts; (4) linear-time encoding/decoding suitable for streaming transfers. The bit-asymmetric K/V quantization insight informs bandwidth-quality tradeoffs for cross-domain cache replication.
source_notes: arXiv v2 published 2026-08-05 (dated August 7, 2026 in paper)
All experiments reproducible from single command on laptop CPU
